DISCREPANCY RESOLVED (2026-07-22): README's 2026-07-14 claim that this needs the separate IOES-Lab/dave sonar-demo branch appears to be incorrect for this checkout -- only references multibeam_sonar_system (present, built, confirmed working) plus ordinary Fuel includes. Smoke-tested: alive 31s, no crash. RE-CHECKED 2026-07-23 for the simulation-progress stall found in dave_multibeam_sonar: sampled /world/oceans_waves/stats (internal world name is 'oceans_waves', same as the base dave_ocean_waves.world, not the filename) for 20s -- sim_time was clearly advancing (41.2s to 43.6s) with RTF frequently near 0.99-1.0, unlike dave_multibeam_sonar's confirmed stall/near-zero pattern. Caveat: the sample was contaminated by a leftover duplicate gz-sim-main instance from an earlier launch attempt in the same terminal session (a second interleaved sim_time/RTF stream with much lower values was also present, real_time offset ~177s ahead) -- the low-RTF stream in that sample cannot be attributed to a specific instance (either instance, or contention between them, could explain it) -- a fully clean single-instance re-sample would be needed for a fully confident number. The contaminated sample confirms that at least one instance progressed (sim_time was clearly advancing, not stalled at zero) -- it does not provide a clean per-instance RTF measurement, and does not confirm this world is free of the same problem multibeam_sonar shows. See notes/results/dave_ocean_waves_sonar.log.

Same sonar-demo-branch resolution as dave_ocean_waves_sonar.world (2026-07-22): multibeam_sonar_system plugin confirmed present/built, no branch dependency. Smoke-tested: alive 32s, no crash. RE-CHECKED 2026-07-23 for the simulation-progress stall found in dave_multibeam_sonar: sampled /world/oceans_waves_sonar_integrated/stats cleanly (single confirmed process, no contamination) for 20s -- sim_time WAS progressing (14.93s to 15.48s, a delta of 0.55s, over a ~20s sampling command), but at a degraded rate -- effective RTF approximately 0.03 by endpoint delta (~30x slower than real time; individual per-message RTF values in the raw log ranged 0.005-0.39 and are noisy/bursty, so treat the endpoint-delta figure as the more defensible estimate, and both as order-of-magnitude only, not precise). Downgraded to PARTIAL: this is not the same total stall as dave_multibeam_sonar, but it is a real, confirmed performance degradation, not yet explained. UPDATE 2026-07-29 (Docker, lyrical-theme-test): fresh clean single-process re-check (PID verified via ps, no contamination), sampled over ~4.5 minutes with 4 sample points 20-40s apart -- iterations increased continuously throughout, never stalled. Delta-based RTF across the samples was consistently in the ~0.1-0.4 range (individual per-message readings noisy, 0.02-0.49), roughly an order of magnitude better than the 2026-07-23 figure of ~0.03. CPU climbed steadily over the observation window (32% at 2min11s elapsed -> 47% at 2min43s -> 69% at 4min37s), not yet plateaued or explained -- this measurement was also taken with two other gz-sim-main instances running concurrently on the same container (a 4h stability test at ~121% CPU and a dave_multibeam_sonar repro at ~33% CPU), an atypical, non-isolated condition, which if anything should have made this result worse, not better, strengthening rather than undermining the improved-RTF finding. Status held at PARTIAL pending a clean isolated re-benchmark and an explanation for the climbing CPU, but the previous RTF ~0.03 figure should not be cited as current -- this world appears meaningfully more usable than previously documented. Worth comparing against dave_multibeam_sonar's exact beam/ray config to see why this world (which shares the same multibeam_sonar_system plugin) performs so much better. See notes/results/dave_ocean_waves_sonar_integrated.log and README.md Progress Log 2026-07-29. UPDATE 2026-08-03 (Mac, Metal, native): first measurement of this world on Mac with the corrected method (wait for sonar init, single confirmed instance, resolved stats topic). RTF 0.2241 on /world/oceans_waves_sonar_integrated/stats (334 msgs, sim +10.989s / real +49.029s, iterations 183449->194438 monotonic). Two prior claims fail. (1) 'The empty scene (dave_multibeam_sonar) is much slower than this heightmap scene' is REFUTED on Mac: the two measure the same, 0.2241 vs 0.19-0.22, despite 5 includes and no ground versus 14 includes plus a Sand Heightmap. That claim rested on two Docker figures (0.0018 / 0.03) and the 0.0018 was withdrawn the same day as a wrong-world measurement. Scene content does not explain the sonar cost, which now looks fixed per frame. (2) The 'CPU climbs 32%->47%->69%' observation is NOT reproduced: after the sonar goes live, 26 consecutive 30s samples over 12.5 minutes oscillate 150.6-201.1% with no upward trend (first half mean 181.0, second half 175.6), and RSS is flat at 279-336 MiB. There is a step at sonar init (~107% -> ~178%) and a ramp before it; the earlier observation was taken with other gz-sim instances running and without separating the startup window. This removes the stated basis for this world's PARTIAL classification -- reclassification not applied here pending a repeat, since this is a single run. Data: notes/results/integrated_isolated_2026-08-03/. Reproduce: MIN=15 bash notes/experiments/exp4_integrated_isolated.sh. UPDATE 2026-08-05 (Mac, re-measured under the stepping criterion): both 2026-08-03 conclusions CONFIRMED. RTF 0.2197 (317 msgs, iterations 173615->183879 monotonic) against 0.2241 before and 0.19-0.22 for the empty multibeam world -- scene content does not explain the sonar cost. CPU flat from the point stepping actually starts (t>=150s, n=26 over 12.5 min): mean 170.7%, first half 172.6 vs second half 168.9, no trend; RSS FALLS 405 -> 281 MiB rather than growing. The 'CPU climbs 32->47->69%' finding remains unreproduced and there is no memory accumulation. Note this run also showed sonar_up flipping at t=60s while CPU held ~107% until t=120s and jumped only at t=150s -- independent confirmation that the sonar log line precedes real work. The stated basis for this world's PARTIAL classification is now unsupported by two independent runs. Data: notes/results/remeasure_2026-08-05/. RECLASSIFIED 2026-08-07 (PARTIAL -> SMOKE PASS): the stated basis for PARTIAL is gone. It rested on two observations, both now refuted. (1) 'RTF ~0.03, a real performance degradation' -- that figure came from a 20s Docker sample on 2026-07-23; Mac measurements under the corrected method give 0.2241 (2026-08-03) and 0.2197 (2026-08-05), i.e. the same as dave_multibeam_sonar's empty scene, so this is the sonar's cost rather than anything specific to this world. (2) 'CPU climbs 32->47->69%' -- not reproduced in two independent isolated runs; CPU is flat over 12.5 minutes (means 172.6 vs 168.9 across halves) and RSS FALLS 405 -> 281 MiB rather than growing. The original observation was taken with two other gz-sim instances on the same container and without separating the startup window. Classified SMOKE PASS, not FUNCTIONAL PASS: process health and sustained stepping are well evidenced, but this world's sonar output topics (PointCloud2 / sonar image) have never been topic-echoed -- only /world/.../stats was read. That matches dave_ocean_waves_sonar.world, the same sonar family, also SMOKE PASS. Note the absolute RTF figures above predate the 2026-08-06 conditions change (Release build, FASTDDS_BUILTIN_TRANSPORTS=UDPv4, corrected settle) and have not been re-measured for this world; the reclassification rests on the CPU/RSS refutation and on parity with the multibeam world, not on the absolute number.
